report.summary: Chunk 11 of 13 of drift.py: validates snapshot internal consistency (counts, phantom entries, test_only, dark_switches, baselined islands, known_unreached, NEW_ISLAND/TEST_ONLY logic).

handoff.purpose: Validate snapshot integrity: count mismatches, phantom entries, test_only subset, dark_switch existence, baselined islands, known_unreached set, and NEW_ISLAND/TEST_ONLY drift items.

claims.text: A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet.
claims.why: The code after this comment performs cross-checks: phantom_islands, phantom for unknown/shim, phantom_test_only, phantom_dark. These verify lists against each other and against the modules list, preventing pre-seeded entries.

claims.text: An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as 'reached' and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in ``modules``. The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: The comment references write_snapshot and acceptance behavior, but this chunk does not contain write_snapshot or the acceptance logic beyond accepted_keys. The baseline behavior and acceptance suppression cannot be verified here.

claims.text: What the BASELINE actually establishes. Intersecting with ``modules`` is the teeth behind the subset rule above: an island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide.
claims.why: The code computes baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules, enforcing the subset rule. Phantom island check earlier also ensures islands are in modules.

claims.text: BECAME ISLAND means 'it was REACHED and is not any more'. A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island.
claims.why: The comment explains the semantic meaning of BECAME ISLAND, but this chunk does not contain the BECAME ISLAND drift item generation. The known_unreached set is computed but not used in this chunk to filter BECAME ISLAND items.

claims.text: The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: This chunk does not show how acceptances are used to suppress or not suppress findings. Only accepted_keys is computed.

observations.what: The known_unreached set includes accepted items with keys starting with 'island', 'unknown', or 'shim', but the comment says 'accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline', yet accepted islands are included in known_unreached via this mechanism.
observations.where: line ~1270: known_unreached = ((old_islands | old_unknown | old_shims) & old_modules) | { k.split(':',1)[1] for k in accepted_keys if k.split(':',1)[0] in ('island','unknown','shim')}

observations.what: The code creates DriftItem with kind=INVALID_SNAPSHOT for phantom entries, but the remedy is always an empty string, which may be incomplete.
